[LINT.4.1] `i1 overlaps i2` is `Bool` and true iff the two
intervals' intersection is non-empty. The intersection of two
half-open intervals is itself half-open, running from the later
start to the earlier end, so the test is that one precedes the
other:

```
i1 overlaps i2  iff  max(i1.start, i2.start) < min(i1.end, i2.end)
```

**This is the definition rather than a consequence of it**, which is
why it is stated over the intersection bounds instead of as a pair
of cross-interval comparisons. An implementation may evaluate the
equivalent conjunction

```
i1.start < i1.end  and  i2.start < i2.end          # both non-empty
    and  i1.start < i2.end  and  i2.start < i1.end
```

but the two non-emptiness conjuncts are **not optional**: without
them the form admits an empty interval lying strictly inside a
non-empty one, which has no instant in common with it
([LINT.7.1]) and therefore does not overlap it.
